wintercity_e02_entry.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_entry.text: On Day 822, the old woman who cleared the inn's breakfast table brought news that the northern footpath had closed for a drainage repair. Yue had intended to walk it to a room advertised near the municipal baths. She changed her route before setting out. The repair did not require a prophecy or an adversary to affect her day. It required a different street, more time, and the decision to carry less while looking for somewhere to stay beyond her first paid interval.

wintercity_e02_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_002.text: Mrs. Fen's introductory common-room allocation would end in three nights. Her ordinary heated-space charge would then apply. Yue thanked her for marking the change before it occurred. A guest could choose a different arrangement while there was still time to move, and the innkeeper could decline to sell warmth below her own costs. The temporary favour remained a favour even though its ending disappointed someone. Yue placed the new charge beside the old receipt so she would not compare unlike weeks.

wintercity_e02_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_003.text: She took the trampling path beside a line of bare fruit trees. The trees stood in stone collars where people could not pile ash against their bark. A municipal gardener was sweeping those collars with a short broom. Yue asked why they were bare before the adjacent hedges. The gardener named the variety and the season. There was no spiritual explanation to discover behind every different leaf. He also told her which gate would lead to the baths without crossing the closed footpath.

wintercity_e02_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_004.text: At the baths, the cheaper washing hour began before dawn and the dearer hour covered the afternoon. Heated water came from a separate allocation, and private bathing rooms cost more than the communal hall. Yue read the entire slate. A clerk could stamp an employment discount only for a contract that actually included it. Her receiving job did not. She bought one ordinary washing token, keeping enough time between the bath and her shift to dry her hair before walking outside.

wintercity_e02_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_005.text: The bath attendant asked her to remove metal ornaments before entering the hot room. Yue tied her pendant inside the inner pocket of her dry robe instead of leaving it on the communal shelf. The object had remained hers through earlier journeys; it neither paid her bill nor supplied an untested technique. Beside her, another woman put a wedding ring into a cloth knot. They watched their own belongings while the attendant checked that the floor mats had not shifted.

wintercity_e02_006.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_006.text: A person in the hot room urged Yue to breathe deeply and gather the rising vapour. She declined without arguing about his practice. Her method required known conditions and a grounded release, not a stranger's claim that warm water carried suitable qi. Ordinary bathing relaxed cold muscles. It could not establish compatibility, replenish a precisely measured reserve, or qualify a new route. Yue rested until her hair had stopped dripping, then dressed in the cooler room where the air did not make her dizzy.

wintercity_e02_007.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_007.text: At the receiving courtyard, Lan had put a red cord across a patch of uneven paving. A cart wheel had caught there the evening before. The repair team would arrive after the shift. Everyone could still reach the scale by a slightly longer path. The cord changed how Yue positioned her counting chair. She did not ask the store workers to carry heavy containers over the defect because the usual route was shorter. An inconvenience noticed before an accident was already useful information.

wintercity_e02_008.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_008.text: The day's largest delivery contained insulating sleeves of two sizes. They shared a wrapper colour and differed only in a little punched mark. Yue asked the carrier to sort them into separate trays before she recorded accepted quantities. He preferred a single total. Lan supported the separation because each size belonged to a different pipe. The count took longer. That delay would matter to the carrier's next appointment, but a quick mixed count would conceal a shortage until the sleeves were installed.

wintercity_e02_009.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_009.text: The carrier sent word to his next customer through a boy who ran messages for a posted fee. The boy asked for the fee before leaving and wrote the destination on a slate. No one described his work as an opportunity to help important people. Yue paid for her own short message to Mrs. Fen, telling her that the amended delivery would make Yue late for the meal collection. Mrs. Fen's kitchen could reserve a portion if the notice arrived in time.

wintercity_e02_010.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_010.text: Lan asked Yue to copy the agreed service calendar into the public summary after the stock had been counted. Only approved dates belonged there. A proposed earlier interruption remained inside the staff folder because it had not been adopted, not because every proposal was too secret to discuss. Yue copied the signed interval and its review contact. A tenant reading the summary could tell when the current supply was expected to stop, and where to ask what arrangements would replace it.

wintercity_e02_011.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_011.text: Three separate housing notices hung near the heat court's gate. One offered a small room in a courtyard whose residents bought a shared evening allocation. One offered a bed in the works' staff annex to people with a short winter appointment, including Yue's receiving contract. The third was Mrs. Fen's ordinary weekly extension. The first two required deposits for different reasons. Yue did not assume that the cheapest bed would have the cheapest exit, or that a deposit meant ownership of anything.

wintercity_e02_012.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_012.text: The courtyard room belonged to a seamstress who would travel to visit her sister during the cold term's first week. She rented it through the residents' clerk, who kept the key inventory. Its occupant would have a vote about that courtyard's shared opening hours while paying its stated share, but no authority over other tenants' private rooms. The roof had recently been mended. The clerk showed the repair receipt without calling it a guarantee against every future leak.

wintercity_e02_013.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_013.text: At the works annex, the steward explained that a bed included access to the staff warming hall during its posted hours. It did not include private apparatus time. Residents had to leave the room within two days after their qualifying work appointment ended, unless a separate paid extension was agreed. Yue asked whether refusing a later factory offer would cancel her present receiving appointment. The steward pointed to the existing terms: completed shifts and the original end date still governed them.

wintercity_e02_014.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_014.text: She requested a copy of the annex departure rule before making any choice. Its deposit covered returned keys and ordinary room damage, with inspection before deductions. It did not secure a worker's obedience. Yet the two-day departure interval could become a practical pressure if another room was hard to find. Yue wrote that consequence beside the price. A contract could preserve formal freedom while arranging circumstances that made the exercise of freedom expensive.

wintercity_e02_015.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_015.text: Mrs. Fen's extension had no connection to the works. It kept Yue in the shared room, offered no residents' vote elsewhere, and cost more once the introductory common-room allocation ended. She could leave on the ordinary notice without waiting for an employer to confirm her status. Mrs. Fen preferred payment a week ahead. Yue asked whether an earlier departure would return any nights. The answer was no under that rate; a daily rate existed, at a higher cost.

wintercity_e02_016.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_016.text: Yue spread the three notices on the inn's table. Rui Wen studied the annex rule because she had once lost time searching for a room after an employer ended a job. Bai Jia preferred the courtyard's shared hours but warned that residents could disagree. They offered experience rather than instructions. Yue had to choose which actual arrangement she could support with her time and money. None would make her a member of every group in the city, or save her from reading later terms.

wintercity_lodging_choice.speaker: narrator
wintercity_lodging_choice.text: She considered the lodging commitment after checking the money available for its deposit and the interval it covered. The commitment would determine where she slept, whose opening hours she could help decide, and whether her room depended on the receiving appointment. It would not increase her reserve or improve her ability to handle hot pipes. She kept the unchosen notices for comparison, with a mark showing that they remained offers she had not accepted.

choices.text: Rent the courtyard room and take its limited residents' vote.
Use the cheaper staff annex with its employment-linked departure date.
Keep the independent inn bed at the higher weekly rate.

wintercity_e02_018.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_018.text: The decision had been made. Whichever lodging arrangement applied, the receiving job retained its limited hours and its end date. Yue packed the papers that needed to travel with her and left the confidential cover closed. A paid bed could be an important source of safety without authorizing new work. The next two days would include another complete shift, an orientation walk, and a request for the cold-term service notices that affected her actual room.

wintercity_e02_019.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_019.text: On Day 823, the public information room displayed a more detailed map than the street model. It showed the producers, distribution sections, return paths, and independent heaters. Some workshops did not buy city heat at all. They burned ordinary fuel in inspected stoves. A missed main allocation would affect them through street conditions and customers rather than by immediately extinguishing their furnaces. Yue could not treat every household as depending on the same valve merely because the pipes crossed the same district.

wintercity_e02_020.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_020.text: Tang Yi guided three newcomers through the map. He asked them to find the public room nearest their lodging, then identify a second route in case its street closed. Yue checked the route physically afterward. One alley on the map was narrower than expected, and a barrow would block it when the butcher received deliveries. She noted a wider route rather than declaring the map useless. An accurate diagram still needed ordinary observations about the people who used its spaces.

wintercity_e02_021.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_021.text: At a bridge junction, a notice named the local isolation key holder and an alternate. The alternate was on duty when Yue passed, a short man with a wool cap and a slow, careful manner. He checked a seal before touching the locked cabinet. Yue watched from outside the working area. He did not open the cabinet to reward her curiosity. The public notice let clients know where to report trouble; it did not convert every passer-by into a permitted emergency operator.

wintercity_e02_022.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_022.text: Two factory apprentices were clearing packed snow from the cabinet's approach, though no new snow had fallen that morning. It had been scraped from a roof above and dumped there overnight. They argued about whose department ought to have prevented it. The alternate asked them to clear the approach first, then record its source for the maintenance meeting. Immediate access and later accountability were distinct tasks. Finishing the first would not make the second unnecessary or prove either department's entire history of blame.

wintercity_e02_023.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_023.text: Yue wanted to help with the spade until she saw how much packed weight each stroke moved. She offered instead to hold the warning board where passers-by could see it. The apprentices accepted. The task ended when the narrow approach was clear and the board had been fixed to a post. She did not charge it to her receiving shift. Nor did she promise to stand there whenever snow fell. A useful small intervention could remain small and complete.

wintercity_e02_024.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_024.text: A children's school stood beside the bridge. Its cloakroom had no direct main connection; a purchased portable heater warmed it for a defined morning interval. Yue saw a teacher turn it off after the last class entered the inner room. The little heater's fuel cartridge would not warm an entire building. Its scale made the distinction visible. Someone who wanted a replacement service after a main closure would need to decide which rooms, which hours, and which people the available supply could actually support.

wintercity_e02_025.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_025.text: The schoolkeeper asked Yi whether the proposed closure would overlap examination day. He showed her the currently approved date and the review contact, not the staff folder's unadopted alternatives. She planned to request a copy for the parents' notice. Yue listened without offering to carry a family's concern as her own mandate. The schoolkeeper knew her timetable, the parents knew their children's travel, and Yue knew only a slice of the city's heating paperwork. Cooperation would need those authorities to remain distinct.

wintercity_e02_026.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_026.text: At the orientation walk's end, Yi brought the group to the municipal inspection office. Its waiting room held rejected applications beside approved ones, with names removed from the public examples. Yue read an application refused because the proposed operator had no examined capacity for the instrument's input. Another had been returned for an incomplete grounding plan. Neither refusal said that the applicants lacked courage. The examples helped her distinguish an incomplete form from a technical limit that a better form could not remove.

wintercity_e02_027.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_027.text: The office's public bench could be booked for a defined small task once the applicant supplied a safe procedure and the fee. It had no standing relationship with her mine papers. An authorized incoming appointment, if she held one, remained a separate instrument and purpose. Yue asked for the public application form without submitting it immediately. She would not let the pleasure of being invited into an office make her promise a test whose supplies and release path she had not yet examined.

wintercity_e02_028.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_028.text: The form asked for the input source, maximum flow, useful output, permitted route, shutdown method, and observer. Yue could answer some lines from her established practice. She could not name a local instrument by guessing from the nearest copper housing. Yi suggested she inspect the public training apparatus on its open day. He made no promise of admission. His advice gave her a practical next step; the inspector would still have to decide whether the proposed application met the actual conditions.

wintercity_e02_029.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_029.text: On Day 824, Lan offered a five-morning extension through Day 828, four paid hours each morning at two copper per hour. The first six-day appointment had ended on Day 822; Yue accepted the separate terms before starting. Her stock comparison found a returned valve seat still inside the accepted subtotal. She corrected that count with Lan witnessing. The physical piece did not reappear, the seller's credit remained pending, and the maintenance team would now have to replace the missing usable part through ordinary purchasing.

wintercity_e02_030.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_030.text: The corrected stock total affected a maintenance order. A team that had expected forty-eight usable seats now had forty-seven. Lan asked them to choose whether to delay one nonurgent replacement or obtain the additional part. They could not repair the shortage by praising the honesty of the correction. The team chose a separately recorded purchase and scheduled its delivery. Yue saw how a seemingly small accurate sentence could change someone's work, with a cost that the sentence itself could not pay.

wintercity_e02_031.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_031.text: At midday, a cold draught crossed the counting table because the loading doors stayed open for delayed carts. Lan let Yue move the paper work inside while the store workers remained at the scale. Yue asked how they would rotate breaks. Lan showed the existing schedule and adjusted one interval around the cart arrivals. The adjustment needed another worker's agreement. A warmer desk could protect Yue's hands without resolving the exposure of the people still waiting outside.

wintercity_e02_032.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_032.text: One worker declined the proposed swap because he had arranged to collect his daughter. Lan accepted that reason and offered a different arrangement. The man did not need to publish his household's entire situation to establish that he could not take the extra interval. Yue recorded the final cart time, not his private explanation. When someone later asked why the schedule had changed, the public answer would identify the amended coverage rather than turn a child into an excuse available for strangers to judge.

wintercity_e02_033.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_033.text: The last receipts were hard to read because rain had reached a carrier's satchel. Yue copied only the lines she could distinguish and set the rest aside for confirmation. The seller's clerk returned with the source duplicate. An hour of delay produced a reliable completed copy. Guessing would have made the book look finished earlier while transferring uncertainty to the maintenance team. Lan signed the completed shift after checking that the unresolved credit had not been mislabelled as paid.

wintercity_e02_034.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_034.text: After work, Yue bought a small quantity of ordinary lamp oil. She did not choose the cheapest bottle until the seller opened one for the smell test he advertised. The oil had a sharp scent unlike the sample described on the slate. He offered a different batch at a different price. She bought less of the second batch. Her practice reserve did not excuse a smoky room, and a spiritual wick was not the right replacement for ordinary light needed to mend her clothes.

wintercity_e02_035.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_035.text: At supper she heard that the cold term's first official allocation would begin on Day 832. Until then, each lodging arrangement relied on its present purchased hours or ordinary stoves. The term's beginning was a service date, not a sudden change in weather. The weather had already made mornings uncomfortable. Yue marked both facts. People could be cold before a contract called the season cold, and a contract could remain payable through a milder afternoon.

wintercity_e02_036.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_036.text: A music student in the dining room was rehearsing a phrase quietly with his fingers on the table. He had rented a practice room near the works because its evening warmth allowed him to hold a bow. The longer contract would cost him less per hour if he stayed for the whole term, but he expected an audition elsewhere. He asked Yue which offer seemed better. She asked how likely the audition journey was and which cost he could bear if he left early.

wintercity_e02_037.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_037.text: He did not know the likelihood, and Yue could not calculate it for him. They compared only the actual exit charges and the money he would need to travel. He chose the shorter arrangement after a long silence. The inn table offered no authority to certify his future. Yet checking the real alternatives let him make a choice that could remain his, even if a later result made him regret the price. Yue wished him luck without converting the wish into a prediction.

wintercity_e02_038.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_038.text: On Day 825, Qiao Ning brought a notice of the first residents' closure-calendar meeting. The meeting would hear clients and staff, with a separate written route for those unable to attend. It would not force a supplier to generate an unlimited allocation. Its task was to identify which proposed intervals could be supported, whose present terms would be affected, and what notice or replacement service was owed. Yue asked whether visitors without local client authority could attend as observers.

wintercity_e02_039.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_039.text: Observers could attend the public portion and read the published minutes. Speaking for a courtyard required that courtyard's own authorization. Speaking about a private works appointment required the relevant person to disclose only what their agreement allowed. A guest could discuss her own inn service, but not convert that into a collective mandate from all guests. Ning marked the three distinctions on the agenda. Yue kept them with the lodging papers that would determine which of those practical positions she actually held.

wintercity_e02_040.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_040.text: The receiving courtyard's final planned cart that morning arrived with a broken outer seal. Lan stopped it outside the enclosed store. The break did not prove that the material was unsafe, but it invalidated one shortcut used in ordinary acceptance. The carrier showed his road report: a fall had damaged the seal, and a local witness had signed the incident. A separate inspection could establish the contents. It would take time and require the seller's approval before opening the inner wrappers.

wintercity_e02_041.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_041.text: Yue copied the incident report without changing its author's uncertain phrase about the cart's angle. The witness had seen it after the fall, not during the instant when the wheel slipped. She knew the difference because the witness said it. A clear account of what someone did not see could prevent a later hearing from making them responsible for a story they had never told. The carrier appreciated the care but still worried about his unpaid waiting hours.

wintercity_e02_042.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_042.text: The seller agreed to the additional inspection and its stated cost. Thirty-two wrapped controls were inside; all thirty-two passed the permitted checks. Lan accepted them under the revised procedure and preserved the broken seal in the incident packet. The carrier's waiting claim went to a different form. Accepting the material did not settle which party owed him time. Yue placed both references on the receipt so a reader could find the linked issues without silently blending their outcomes.

wintercity_e02_043.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_043.text: In the afternoon, Yi showed Yue the training apparatus she might later request. Its copper thread ran through an enclosed indicator and ended at an inspected grounded wick. The external test supply was optional for a demonstration, but necessary for the particular coupled task described on the public board. Yue would have to inspect its compatibility and account for its discharge separately from her own half-unit input. The apparatus had no heating outlet connected to occupied rooms. A failure could spoil the test without leaving a household cold.

wintercity_e02_044.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_044.text: The public open day allowed observation, not an unsupervised attempt. Yue stood behind the line while an instructor demonstrated the shutoff. She watched the ordinary isolation lever, the permitted control signal, and the indicator that showed the charge had drained. They served different purposes. The instructor then asked the audience which one to trust if the indicator failed. Yue answered that the ordinary isolation and measured discharge procedure still applied, while a failed indicator required the apparatus to remain out of use until inspected.

wintercity_e02_045.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_045.text: The instructor asked whether she wanted to book a later demonstration. Yue said she first needed to complete her arrival duties and confirm her available funds. He handed her a dated fee schedule. Fees could change next term, so she would have to check again before paying. The schedule gave her enough information to plan. It did not claim her next appointment before she had chosen it, and no one suggested borrowing against wages that had not yet been earned.

wintercity_e02_046.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_046.text: That evening she measured the time the different city journeys required. The heat court to the baths took eighteen unhurried minutes. The public information room to her ordinary letter collection took another twelve. Her actual lodging route differed according to the commitment she had made. She recorded the route she used, leaving the others as references. A schedule built from a map's apparent closeness could fail even when every address was right, because walking and safe crossings still consumed time.

wintercity_e02_047.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_047.text: She prepared the first next-week expense estimate with ranges instead of certainty. Lodging was governed by her selected terms; meals depended on how many shifts kept her away from the kitchen; the possible practice appointment still required a separate choice. She left an ordinary travel reserve untouched. That reserve would not pay for an unlimited emergency, but it gave her a way to leave a room without immediately promising new labour to its owner. She had learned to value exits that could actually be used.

wintercity_e02_048.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_048.text: On Day 826, the receiving work started early. A new clerk named Diao Chen came to compare the returned-stock account. He read quickly and initially treated an unresolved credit as a completed refund. Yue showed him the signed entry and the pending form. He crossed out his annotation before the summary went onward. His error was ordinary, not proof that the whole office conspired against carriers. Leaving its correction visible would let a later reader understand why the summary changed.

wintercity_e02_049.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_049.text: Chen asked whether Yue intended to join the works permanently. She said she had accepted only the six-day counting appointment so far. He remarked that permanent staff got better heat prices. Yue asked which obligations went with the prices. He did not have the employment forms at his desk, and admitted it. They continued the stock comparison. A favourable rumour could be worth investigating without serving as a contract, and an office acquaintance could be helpful without becoming her private recruiter.

wintercity_e02_050.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_050.text: The shift ended with four hours of completed stock work entered for payment under the arrival appointment. Yue checked the record against her actual scheduled hours. An amended interval from the orientation day remained shorter; today's full interval did not compensate it by magic. She kept the copies in order. She would eventually need a single payment receipt, but the individual hours mattered if the final total differed. A total was an answer whose components still needed to exist.

wintercity_e02_051.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_051.text: After the shift, she visited the municipal library's public shelf. The city's charter used borrowed winter as the name of a financial arrangement: factories sold guaranteed cold-term allocations in advance, and clients borrowed against later production to pay early. The phrase had also become a poet's name for the basin. Yue could appreciate the poem while reading the interest provisions. A metaphor made the city memorable; it could not tell a tenant whether borrowing for heat would leave a food budget intact.

wintercity_e02_052.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_052.text: Several public forms offered instalments without requiring an employer's endorsement. Their eligibility depended on a stated income interval and guarantor rules. Yue read them but did not apply. She had no reason yet to take a heat loan beyond the arrangement she had already chosen. The fact that a form existed did not mean its risk was appropriate for her. She copied the office address for someone who might need it, rather than copy a stranger's claim that no one would be refused.

wintercity_e02_053.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_053.text: A man at the neighbouring shelf asked her to read his form aloud because the smaller print defeated his eyes. Yue did so without keeping a copy. The form tied a reduced price to a longer commitment. He asked about a clause permitting a service pause for maintenance. She read its replacement-service obligation next. He had mistaken a pause for an unconditional cancellation of heat, and felt less frightened after seeing the actual clause. Yet he still had to decide whether the longer price suited his household.

wintercity_e02_054.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_054.text: The librarian found the public definition of replacement service. It meant access to stated communal hours during approved maintenance, with exceptions and a review process. It did not promise every household a portable heater. Yue read the qualification aloud too. The man chose to take the form home before signing. A full explanation had made the offer less alarming in one respect and less generous in another. Both changes belonged to the same honest reading, rather than whichever version would persuade him.

wintercity_e02_055.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_055.text: At dusk a public room queue extended around a corner. One keeper asked people to leave a gap for the bath cart. Yue waited in that gap until another guest pointed out the queue's actual continuation. She moved to the end. Being new made the mistake understandable without giving her priority over those who had waited. The keeper eventually opened the second room, funded for that day's additional hours after the first reached capacity. Its door displayed the separate closing time.

wintercity_e02_056.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_056.text: Inside, Yue listened to a pair of elderly men compare the old hillside charcoal shops with the new distribution main. One preferred the independence of a stove; the other preferred not carrying sacks upstairs. Neither version served every household. The first man's house had an inspected chimney; the second's room did not. Yue asked whether chimney inspection was costly, and learned where the public assistance application could be found. She left with a question about who could actually use an apparent alternative.

wintercity_e02_057.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_057.text: On Day 827, she bought a small notebook for city service questions. Her old expense book remained for money, and her practice pages for measured capacities. Combining everything into one impressive ledger would make it harder to answer an ordinary request quickly. She could afford the notebook because the completed counting shifts had established a finite payment due, though she still would not spend that due as though it had been collected. The purchase came from the cash already available for city expenses.

wintercity_e02_058.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_058.text: She spent the afternoon reading public notices near the housing clerk. Some described past closures, with dates and actual replacement hours; others advertised proposed improvements not yet funded. The distinction was printed clearly on most, but one old advertisement had faded until its future tense was hard to see. Yue asked the clerk whether it still applied. He took it down and put up the approved current notice. That simple act corrected a possible false expectation without needing a tribunal.

wintercity_e02_059.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_059.text: A small crowd waited for him to finish. One woman wanted the previous advertisement preserved because she had relied on its claim when signing a contract. He placed it in the complaint file rather than discard it. Yue saw why tidying a wall could not justify destroying evidence. The current notice needed to replace the old one in public use; the old one still mattered to someone whose earlier decision had been shaped by it. Different purposes required different custody.

wintercity_e02_060.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_060.text: The woman's complaint concerned a promised laundry-room allocation. Yue did not ask to see the private contract. She noted the public form number after the woman consented to its being mentioned without a name. If the question arose at the calendar meeting, the actual complainant could choose whether to speak or send a written account. Yue could identify a public service issue without claiming a second person's loss as her own experience. The distinction slowed conversation but kept agency where it belonged.

wintercity_e02_061.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_061.text: At supper, Jia described her day's choice to drop the fourth shop from her delivery route. The shop bought irregularly and expected free returns. Losing its possible sales shortened her route and reduced spoiled beans. Yue admired the calculation but did not call it a universal lesson about refusing expansion. Jia might choose differently if the shop changed its terms. Their conversation mattered because a business owner's own limits were visible, not because Yue could turn another woman's livelihood into an allegory of cultivation.

wintercity_e02_062.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_062.text: Wen returned with a partial umbrella payment and a written date for the remainder. She looked relieved and frustrated together. Yue asked whether she wanted company on the next visit. Wen said no; she would take her own apprentice, who knew the order. That refusal cost their friendship nothing. Yue offered tea instead. Helping did not require becoming indispensable, and a companion's reasonable decision to choose somebody else could remain part of an evening that ended warmly.

wintercity_e02_063.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_063.text: On Day 828, the cold-term board received its last approved opening times before the initial service began. Yue compared them with the copies she already held. Two public rooms had changed hours, with the amendment signed and the earlier notice retained for reference. Her actual lodging arrangement would determine which room mattered most to her evening. She planned that route without promising every other visitor the same access. A city's common infrastructure reached people through particular doors and particular schedules.

wintercity_e02_064.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_064.text: She took the new calendar to Lan, who wanted it posted beside the staff exit. Lan approved the public copy and asked Yue to leave room beneath it for later amendments. The space was useful because certainty would not last. Yue wrote the effective date prominently. A reader should not have to infer which winter an old sheet described, or whether a handwritten change overruled the printed line. Legibility could not settle a dispute, but poor legibility could create one unnecessarily.

wintercity_e02_065.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e02_065.text: Her preparation interval ended with an actual place to sleep, a finite receiving appointment nearly completed, and the beginning of a usable city map. The cold term would start after those beginnings, with different people expecting different things from it. Yue had not yet run the city's apparatus, won an employer's favour, or secured a permanent place. She stood at the court gate with tomorrow's work list in her hand, ready to count the next delivery before making any larger promise.

wintercity_lodging_court.speaker: narrator
wintercity_lodging_court.text: Yue took the courtyard room. The clerk counted a six-copper key deposit and an eight-copper first-week rent, then let her inspect the latch before signing. The shared evening heat share was separate and would be collected before the cold term began. She obtained a vote only for this courtyard's purchased hours, with the tenants' posted procedure. She could not claim that vote before moving in or use it to speak for another street.

wintercity_lodging_court_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_lodging_court_002.text: The seamstress had left a shelf empty for the visitor's possessions. Yue put her lamp there and moved the washbasin away from the bedding. Two neighbours helped carry the trunk in exchange for the ordinary lifting fee. By dusk, she had returned Mrs. Fen's key and received her inspection receipt. The new room gave her privacy, a cheaper nightly cost, and a practical duty to participate in the courtyard's finite service arrangements.

wintercity_lodging_court_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_lodging_court_003.text: In the courtyard meeting book, she entered her own name as the temporary occupant, leaving the absent seamstress's ownership unchanged. She copied the next residents' meeting time. Its hours would compete with her work, and she would have to arrange attendance. Her vote ended when she returned the key.

wintercity_lodging_works.speaker: narrator
wintercity_lodging_works.text: Yue accepted the works annex bed. She paid its four-copper key deposit and six-copper first-week charge. The steward entered the end of her qualifying receiving appointment and the two-day departure window beside her name. Its warming hall would be available during the staff hours, but no private apparatus bench came with the bed. Yue asked where she could keep a confidential paper; he showed the lockable compartment, whose key remained part of the return inventory.

wintercity_lodging_works_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_lodging_works_002.text: She moved after her shift. The room was shared with a filter cleaner who rose before dawn and a delivery clerk who returned late. They agreed how to close the shutter without waking each other. Yue did not mistake their friendliness for an endorsement by the works. She returned the inn key and kept the inspection receipt. Her cheaper bed now depended on a finite employment interval; that fact would shape how readily she could refuse a later offer.

wintercity_lodging_works_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_lodging_works_003.text: Before sleeping, she wrote the ordinary public-room route beside the staff-hall route. If her qualifying job ended, she needed another place to sit warm and another bed rather than a promise.

wintercity_lodging_independent.speaker: narrator
wintercity_lodging_independent.text: Yue extended her bed at Mrs. Fen's inn for twelve copper under the weekly rate. She paid no employer-linked deposit and gained no courtyard vote. The common-room hours and their price were written separately from the bed. Her independence cost more than either alternative's first week. She accepted that cost because the ordinary notice gave her a departure route that did not depend on a works clerk confirming the end of a job.

wintercity_lodging_independent_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_lodging_independent_002.text: Mrs. Fen moved her trunk to a less draughty corner after another guest departed. Yue paid the stated lifting fee rather than carry it upstairs herself. Wen helped her pin the drying labels where they would remain readable. She kept her own lamp and papers in the shared room, locking the confidential cover inside her trunk. The inn arrangement gave no private apparatus access, collective mandate, or employment discount.

wintercity_lodging_independent_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_lodging_independent_003.text: She crossed out the other offered lodging dates in her diary without destroying their notices. Later she could compare service terms as an actual inn guest, but she could not offer a vote belonging to residents elsewhere.
